title: LRU Cache
corePattern: Hash Map plus Doubly-Linked List for O(1) access with recency ordering
interviewTips: Ask if get and put must both be O(1) average, what capacity range is expected, and whether to return -1 for missing keys.
Trade-off: list plus map is simple but O(n) moves; hash map plus doubly-linked list gives O(1) by splicing nodes via pointers.
Edge-case tip: handle capacity 0, updating existing key without eviction, evicting true LRU on full cache, and keeping map and list strictly in sync.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force with Map plus Recency List
approaches.intuition: Keep values in a hash map for lookup and keep keys in order of use. On every access move the key to most-recently-used end, and on overflow evict the least-recently-used front. Moving in a list costs linear scan.
approaches.theory: Maintain invariant: order[0] is LRU, order[-1] is MRU, and map holds key to value. get: if missing return -1 else remove key from order O(n) and append O(1). put: if exists remove old position O(n), else if full pop front O(n) and delete from map O(1), then insert and append. Correct because every use refreshes recency and eviction always removes oldest.

timeComplexity.explanation: Removing a key from list or LinkedList requires linear scan to find it, where n is current size bounded by capacity. Hash map ops are O(1) average.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Store at most capacity entries in map plus at most capacity keys in recency list.

dryRunExample.input: capacity=2, put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1), put(3,3), get(2), get(3)
steps: get 1: hit, move 1 to end -> order [2,1], return 1
put 3: full, evict order[0]=2 -> map {1:1,3:3}, order [1,3]

edgeCases: capacity 1: every new put evicts previous
put existing key updates value and becomes MRU without eviction
get missing key returns -1 and does not change order
capacity 0: all puts no-op, all gets -1

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Hash Map plus Doubly Linked List
approaches.intuition: Need both O(1) lookup and O(1) reorder and eviction. Use hash map from key to list node, and doubly-linked list with MRU near head and LRU near tail. Splice nodes by rewiring prev and next pointers.
approaches.theory: Use dummy head and tail to avoid null checks. Invariant: head.next is MRU, tail.prev is LRU, map points to live nodes. get: lookup node, if found detach and insert after head. put: if found update value and move to front; else if full detach tail.prev and erase its key, then create node, map it, insert after head. All pointer updates are constant time, so both ops are O(1) average.

code.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, key=0, val=0):
        self.key = key
        self.val = val
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cache = {}
        self.head = Node()
        self.tail = Node()
        self.head.next = self.tail
        self.tail.prev = self.head
    def _remove(self, node):
        p = node.prev
        n = node.next
        p.next = n
        n.prev = p
    def _add_to_front(self, node):
        node.next = self.head.next
        node.prev = self.head
        self.head.next.prev = node
        self.head.next = node
    def get(self, key: int) -> int:
        if key not in self.cache:
            return -1
        node = self.cache[key]
        self._remove(node)
        self._add_to_front(node)
        return node.val
    def put(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        if self.capacity == 0:
            return
        if key in self.cache:
            node = self.cache[key]
            node.val = value
            self._remove(node)
            self._add_to_front(node)
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                lru = self.tail.prev
                self._remove(lru)
                del self.cache[lru.key]
            node = Node(key, value)
            self.cache[key] = node
            self._add_to_front(node)

timeComplexity.complexity: O(1) average per get and put
timeComplexity.explanation: Hash map lookup plus constant pointer rewiring to remove and insert after dummy head. No traversal.

spaceComplexity.explanation: One map entry and one list node per cached key plus two dummy nodes.

dryRunExample.input: capacity=2, put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1), put(3,3), get(2), put(4,4), get(1), get(3), get(4)
steps: get 1: move 1 to front -> head-1-2-tail return 1
get 1: miss -> -1, get 3: hit -> 3, get 4: hit -> 4

edgeCases: capacity 1: put always evicts tail.prev before insert
repeated put on same key updates value and moves to front
get on missing key leaves structure unchanged
large sequential puts: each eviction removes exactly one LRU
